body: Mined the log directly, found 3 real things you need to know. (1) URGENT: your M1 switch already happened but failed -- chart changed correctly, but the new M1 attach only had 1024 bars loaded (needs 5000+), so it refused to start. Press Home on the M1 chart to force-load more history, then reattach. (2) NEW: the 22:03 session (tonight's own WARRANT#95 test, which I stopped actively watching after you announced the M1 switch) actually hit 'shutdown by timeout' then 'Abnormal termination' at 22:54, about 52 seconds into Phase 5 -- I never saw this live. Confirmed via grep that neither phrase exists anywhere in TUNGSTEN's own code -- this is MT4's OWN watchdog force-killing a script that blocked too long without yielding, not a TUNGSTEN bug. (3) Strong lead on why: every other heavy calibration loop has periodic Sleep(1) yields (a known prior fix for exactly this), but Phase 5's two sub-functions have ZERO of them -- the only phase missing that pattern. Didn't fix it yet -- need to read both functions in full first, not guess. On the actual ask: ran the forge-organism 11-step charter against all 3 calibration cycles this log contains. Steps 1-3 are all that's computable from static log data. PBO-CSCV across all 3 cycles clusters right at 0.53, basically the coin-flip line. Ghost gate found 0-1 qualifying OOS trades against the charter's own required minimum of 100 in every cycle that reached Phase 6. Per the charter's OWN rule, that's the stop-and-report condition -- steps 4-11 would mean building on top of a result the charter itself says isn't validated yet. Didn't push past that. Everything's in the memory files and ledger (pass_84), zero code changed this pass -- this was pure log analysis.
